items.q: HMG-CoA reductase reduces 3-hydroxy-3-methylglutaryl-CoA into mevalonate. How many molecules of NADPH are consumed during this rate-limiting committed step of cholesterol synthesis?
items.exp: HMG-CoA reductase performs a two-step reduction of HMG-CoA to mevalonate, consuming two molecules of NADPH and releasing one molecule of free coenzyme A (CoA-SH).
r: Correct. 2 NADPH molecules are consumed per mevalonate synthesized.
Incorrect. 1 NADPH is insufficient for the four-electron reduction.
Incorrect. 3 NADPH is not the stoichiometric ratio.
Incorrect. Only 2 NADPH are required.

o: Sterol binding to Insig-1 promotes recruitment of membrane E3 ubiquitin ligases (gp78 / Trc8) that polyubiquitinate HMG-CoA reductase
High cholesterol binds the active site as an irreversible suicide substrate
Sterols stimulate lysosomal endocytosis of ER membranes
AMPK dephosphorylates HMGCR to trigger cleavage
items.exp: HMG-CoA reductase contains a membrane-spanning sterol-sensing domain. Excess sterols promote binding to Insig, which recruits E3 ubiquitin ligases, polyubiquitinating HMG-CoA reductase for 26S proteasomal destruction.
r: Correct. Sterols induce Insig-mediated ubiquitination and proteasomal degradation of HMGCR.
Incorrect. Cholesterol does not act as a suicide inhibitor.
Incorrect. It is degraded by 26S proteasomes via ERAD, not lysosomes.
Incorrect. AMPK phosphorylates and inactivates HMGCR.

items.q: Statins lower circulating LDL cholesterol primarily by which physiological mechanism?
o: Depleting intracellular hepatocyte cholesterol, which triggers SREBP-2 translocation to induce LDL receptor expression
Directly binding and degrading circulating ApoB-100 particles in blood
Inhibiting intestinal cholesterol absorption via NPC1L1 transporter
Increasing biliary bile salt secretion into feces
items.exp: By competitively inhibiting HMG-CoA reductase, statins reduce hepatocyte intracellular cholesterol. The sterol deficit prompts SREBP-2 translocation to the nucleus, inducing cell-surface LDL receptor synthesis and clearing atherogenic LDL from blood.
r: Correct. Statins upregulate hepatic LDL receptors via SREBP-2 by depleting intracellular cholesterol.
Incorrect. Statins do not directly degrade ApoB.
Incorrect. Ezetimibe inhibits NPC1L1, not statins.
Incorrect. Bile acid sequestrants increase fecal bile excretion.

items.q: Which enzyme catalyzes the initial rate-limiting hydroxylation step in the classical hepatic pathway converting cholesterol into primary bile acids?
items.exp: Cholesterol 7-alpha-hydroxylase (CYP7A1) is an ER cytochrome P450 enzyme that catalyzes the rate-limiting step in primary bile acid synthesis (cholic acid and chenodeoxycholic acid). It is subject to feedback inhibition by bile acids via FXR.
r: Correct. CYP7A1 (Cholesterol 7-alpha-hydroxylase) is the rate-limiting enzyme of bile acid synthesis.
Incorrect. CYP27A1 operates in the alternative pathway.
Incorrect. HMGCR synthesizes cholesterol.
Incorrect. CYP17A1 operates in adrenal steroidogenesis.

items.q: A female infant presents on day 10 of life with ambiguous genitalia, severe dehydration, hyponatremia, and hyperkalemia. Plasma 17-hydroxyprogesterone is markedly elevated. Which enzyme is deficient?
items.exp: 21-hydroxylase deficiency accounts for >90% of congenital adrenal hyperplasia. Failure to convert 17-OHP to 11-deoxycortisol causes cortisol and aldosterone deficiency (salt wasting, shock) and shunts precursors into androgens (virilization).
r: Correct. 21-hydroxylase deficiency causes salt-wasting CAH with elevated 17-OHP and virilization.
Incorrect. 11-beta-hydroxylase deficiency accumulates 11-DOC, causing hypertension, not salt wasting.
Incorrect. 17-alpha-hydroxylase deficiency causes hypokalemia, hypertension, and feminization.
Incorrect. 3-beta-HSD deficiency causes elevated DHEA.
items.kp: 21-hydroxylase (CYP21A2) deficiency is the most common CAH, presenting with salt-wasting crisis (hyponatremia, hyperkalemia) and ambiguous genitalia due to accumulated 17-hydroxyprogesterone shunted into androgens.

items.q: Which enzyme deficiency in congenital adrenal hyperplasia produces virilization in female infants accompanied by severe early-onset hypertension due to accumulation of 11-deoxycorticosterone (11-DOC)?
items.exp: 11-beta-hydroxylase deficiency prevents conversion of 11-DOC to corticosterone and 11-deoxycortisol to cortisol. Accumulated 11-DOC has potent mineralocorticoid activity, causing low-renin hypertension and hypokalemia, alongside androgen virilization.

Incorrect. 21-hydroxylase deficiency causes hypotension and salt wasting.
Incorrect. 17-alpha-hydroxylase deficiency causes female external genitalia in males and lack of virilization.
Incorrect. Aromatase converts androgens to estrogens.

items.q: What transport protein mediates the rate-limiting entry of free cholesterol from the outer mitochondrial membrane into the inner mitochondrial matrix to initiate steroidogenesis?
items.exp: StAR protein translocates cholesterol across the intermembrane space to the inner mitochondrial membrane, where CYP11A1 (desmolase) resides. Mutations in StAR cause lethal congenital lipoid adrenal hyperplasia.
r: Correct. StAR protein mediates the rate-limiting mitochondrial import of cholesterol for steroidogenesis.
Incorrect. CPT-1 transports fatty acylcarnitines.
Incorrect. VDAC transports small metabolites non-specifically.
Incorrect. ABCA1 exports cholesterol at the plasma membrane.

items.q: Farnesyl pyrophosphate (FPP) is a key intermediate in the cholesterol biosynthetic pathway. Which cellular process relies on FPP and its derivative geranylgeranyl pyrophosphate to anchor signaling proteins (such as Ras and Rho) to the inner leaflet of the plasma membrane?
items.exp: FPP and GGPP provide hydrophobic 15- and 20-carbon isoprenoid tails that prenyltransferases attach to C-terminal CAAX cysteines of Ras and Rho GTPases, anchoring them to membranes for active signaling.

Incorrect. O-glycosylation adds sugars in Golgi.
Incorrect. Ubiquitination is for degradation.

items.q: What is the primary mechanism of action of ezetimibe in the treatment of hypercholesterolemia?
o: Selective inhibition of the Niemann-Pick C1-Like 1 (NPC1L1) transporter in the jejunal brush border

Binding of bile acids in the intestinal lumen to prevent reabsorption

Incorrect. Cholestyramine binds bile acids.
Incorrect. Evolocumab and alirocumab inhibit PCSK9.

items.q: Evolocumab and alirocumab are monoclonal antibodies that lower LDL cholesterol by >50-60%. What protein do they inhibit to prevent the lysosomal degradation of cell-surface LDL receptors?
items.exp: PCSK9 normally binds the LDL receptor on the cell surface and escorts it into lysosomes for degradation upon endocytosis. Inhibiting PCSK9 prevents receptor destruction, recycling LDLR back to the surface to maximize LDL clearance.

Incorrect. ApoB-100 is the structural protein on LDL.
Incorrect. MTTP assembles lipoproteins.
Incorrect. CETP transfers cholesteryl esters between lipoproteins.
